These were made by Sandy Law of Wimbledon, a shoemaker and member of the club. In the 1920's Bill Fish was general factotem of the club, preparing the track, knocking in the spikes to tape the lanes in the hundred.

Sandy Law closes up his shoe making business to move to Eastbourne. For many years athletes have gone to Sandy's shop in Revelstoke, Road Wimbledon for a pair of hand made to measure running shoes, possibly his most famous customer being Roger Bannister, the first man to run a mile in under four minutes.

Foster's had superseded Law's as the foremost made-to-measure shoemaker in England when Sandy Law declined to compromise his principles by getting involved with what he regarded as the poor quality footwear of Adidas and Puma.
